entry.content:

Armin Ronacher argues that Rust's mutex poisoning should be removed or made an exception rather than the default behavior. While the feature was designed to signal broken invariants after a panic, the author asserts that it is rarely handled correctly in practice and often results in "slow outages" where a single panic on one thread makes a shared mutex permanently unusable for all subsequent threads.

The article highlights how `PoisonError` can cause deadlocks because it holds the lock, citing issues in projects like RLS and Mozilla, as well as crates like Deno and Polars. Ronacher suggests making `std::sync::nonpoison` the default for `std::sync::Mutex` and introducing an opt-in `Poison<T>` wrapper for users who specifically need to detect poisoned states.

Direct connection to his MacBook Pro yielded full speeds, pointing to a performance bottleneck introduced by the display's USB hub.

Further investigation revealed that the Realtek RTL8156B adapter dropped frames under high loads because its small USB burst size of four packets caused buffer overflows when combined with the hub's round-trip latency. Replacing it with a newer adapter using the RTL8157 chip, which supports an eight-packet burst size, eliminated the frame drops and restored full download performance without requiring network flow control.

The committee will continue developing C++29 at its next full meeting in Istanbul, Turkey, in March 2027.

entry.title: Antithesis Formally Verifies Raft Implementations Using AI and TLA+
entry.content:
Links: antithesis.com | lobsters

Antithesis researchers Rohan Padhye and Hillel Wayne have demonstrated a formal verification paradigm for distributed systems, applying AI, TLA+, and trace validation to production Raft implementations in etcd and HashiCorp. By iteratively model-checking specifications, testing with the Antithesis platform, and constructing mathematical proofs in Lean and TLAPS, the team established core safety properties like Election Safety and Leader Completeness for both libraries.

The collaborative workflow uncovered several previously unknown and open bugs across both codebases, leading to patches that align the implementations with their formal models. While the verification process relies on certain environment assumptions and excludes certain features like complex membership changes or timing-dependent reads, the approach successfully bridges the gap between high-level specifications and production-grade concurrent software.
